title: cross-border-quarantine-playbook-and-test-scenarios
summary: Operator-oriented playbook for quarantining tenant data that crosses regional boundaries or triggers cross-border compliance flags, plus a compact set of test scenarios to validate behavior in staging. Emphasis on minimizing customer disruption while preserving audit evidence for legal review.
purpose: Provide a repeatable operator/runbook for identifying, isolating, communicating, and (if required) deleting data that violates a tenant's pinned-region or a jurisdictional assertion. Includes stepwise playbook, telemetry checklist, and test cases for CI/staging runs.
scope: Applies to Redwood Private and Dedicated tenants with explicit region pins, customers under contractual data residency constraints, and automated routing exceptions. Does NOT cover on-prem air-gapped customers (separate procedures).
definitions: Quarantine: temporary logical isolation of data and request routing to prevent further cross-border write or read access. Legal hold: stop-any-deletion state for specific artifacts pending counsel. Anchor region: customer-declared primary region pin. Transit window: short period while requests are evaluated and rerouted.
assumptions: Service can tag requests and objects with region metadata in telemetry. Operator has access to KMS/Audit bundles. There is a reachable legal contact for urgent holds. Automated routing can switch to fallback model variants within 60s.
high_level_flow: 1) Signal detection (telemetry/alert) 2) Verify event and scope 3) Deploy quarantine policy (routing + storage flag) 4) Notify customer & legal 5) Collect evidence bundle 6) Remediate (reroute, move, delete) 7) Validate and close
quarantine_runbook: Step 0 — Triage: Confirm alert source (telemetry ID, tenant id, object ids). Cross-check with pin map and recent config changes.
Step 1 — Scope determination: Determine whether event affects reads, writes, or both; list impacted blobs/keys/sessions with IDs.
Step 2 — Apply logical quarantine: Add quarantine tag to affected objects and update routing policy for tenant to 'region-isolate' mode (no cross-region reads/writes).
Step 3 — Short-circuit downstream: If request-forwarders still route to other regions, apply temporary deny rules at edge proxies for the tenant-id until reroute completes.

Step 4 — Preserve evidence: Snapshot relevant logs, object checksums, KMS metadata, and produce a signed evidence package (timestamped). Store in evidence-bucket in anchor-region with legal-hold flag.
Step 5 — Customer & legal notification: Use templated emails + support channel; include preliminary impact assessment and expected timeline.

Step 6 — Decide remediation path: Options = (A) immediate rollback/move to anchor region, (B) delete objects under documented consent, (C) escalate to legal hold pending investigation. Record decision in incident ticket.
Step 7 — Implement remediation: Use migration worker to copy and validate content to anchor-region, or run erasure worker if deletion chosen. Ensure checksums and access logs are recorded.
Step 8 — Post-check: Run end-to-end tests for tenant API in anchor-region, confirm latency and integrity, and remove quarantine tag when safe.
Step 9 — Close loop: Deliver final report to customer and legal with timeline, evidence bundle id, and lessons learned.
Operator notes: Keep quarantine window minimal (target < 4 hours). If > 24 hours, require exec-level signoff and legal review. Prefer non-destructive moves when possible.
deletion_runbook: Precondition: Confirm retention/deletion predicates (contract, retention policy, legal hold absence).
Step 1 — Verify consent: Check for explicit deletion consent or absence of legal hold flags. Document proof (support ticket id / signed request).
Step 2 — Prepare deletion plan: Identify object keys, parent resources, and dependent artifacts (indices, caches, replicas).
Step 3 — Snapshot evidence: Archive checksums and metadata in evidence store before deletion. Evidence must include timestamps, operator id, and signed hash.
Step 4 — Schedule deletion window: Prefer low-traffic window and notify customer + SRE.
Step 5 — Execute irreversable deletion: Run certified erasure job that zeroes object on physical storage and removes keys. Record job id and summary.
Step 6 — Confirm and audit: Validate objects are unreachable, run verification scans, and attach results to incident ticket.
Step 7 — Finalize: Update customer and legal; remove any temporary quarantine artifacts.
escalation_matrix: Level 1 — Operator (oncall): initial triage and quarantine apply
Level 2 — Senior SRE/Platform Eng: remediation plan and migration worker approval
Level 3 — Legal + Compliance: legal hold decision, evidence requirements
Level 4 — Product + VP Eng: cross-tenant impact, SLA/contract exceptions
telemetry_and_signals: minimal_evidence_set: request-id, tenant-id, object-ids, pre/post checksums, timestamped route traces
SLI/metrics to track: quarantine-duration, migration-success-rate, customer-impacted-requests
acceptance_tests: Test A — Simulated cross-border write: generate synthetic request that writes from wrong-region, assert quarantine applied within 60s and evidence package exists.
Test B — Concurrent reads blocked: after quarantine, verify reads from non-anchor region return 403 and are logged.
Test C — Migration worker integrity: copy 2500 small objects to anchor region, validate checksums and access patterns; run in staging with throttling.
Test D — Legal hold resilience: place legal hold mid-migration and confirm deletion is prevented and evidence preserved.
Test E — Operator failover: primary operator applies quarantine then goes offline; verify second operator can pick up idempotently and continue.
Test F — Telemetry sampling fidelity: intentionally trigger 100 cross-border events and validate 95%+ have full evidence bundle attached.
known_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Migration exceeds TTL and blocks customer traffic. Mitigation: progressive migration with throttled reads fallback and customer communication template.
Risk: Evidence package missing KMS metadata due to permission boundary. Mitigation: pre-authorize evidence-role and include KMS backup export step.
Risk: Accidental mass-delete. Mitigation: two-person approval for irreversible deletion and dry-run mode that lists impacted keys.
Risk: False positive quarantine floods. Mitigation: debounce alerts and require 2 independent signals before automatic quarantine in non-blocking mode.
timeline_and_rollout_notes: Pilot in staging for two tenants in eu-west-1 in Q1; iterate test cases and then gate to limited production for customers with strict region pins. Add training session for oncall and run tabletop exercises. Target automated quarantine toggle flag for 2025-02 release.
open_questions: Do we need a separate immutable evidence store for EU/UK regulatory audits?
Should quarantine be automatic for high-confidence signals or always operator-confirmed?
What SLA credit model applies if quarantine causes >2% additional latency for redirected traffic?
How do we surface quarantine status to customer dashboards without exposing internal incident details?
